outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has moved: Chen, Ghomi and Wang posted preprints claiming the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard manifolds in dimension 5 (10 Sep 2026) and in dimensions 3 to 9 (17 Sep 2026), both acknowledging Claude and ChatGPT, while other 2025-2026 preprints prove the inequality only under pinching, in a restricted class of manifolds, or locally, and the 2019 Ghomi-Spruck claim for all dimensions has a reported gap and is treated as open by later sources.
problem_asks: (1) For a complete simply connected Riemannian n-manifold M of nonpositive sectional curvature (a Cartan-Hadamard manifold) and a subset Ω of M, the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality holds: the boundary measure of Ω is at least that of a Euclidean ball of the same volume, i.e. |∂Ω|^n / |Ω|^(n-1) is at least its Euclidean value. The bullet says 'subsets' without restricting to bounded domains or finite perimeter; the standard formulations (as in the sources read) use bounded sets of finite perimeter and positive volume. (2) That this holds for every Cartan-Hadamard manifold in every dimension n: the bullet quantifies over spaces of nonpositive curvature and does not restrict n. (3) The bullet asks whether the inequality can be extended, so either a proof for all such M and n, or a counterexample, would decide it. (4) The equality case (equality only for a Euclidean ball) is part of the standard formulation per the Wikipedia article's precise statement, though it is not in the bullet text.

events.what_happened: André Weil proved the isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard surfaces (dimension 2, Gauss curvature K <= 0) in 1926 ('Sur les surfaces à courbure négative', Comptes Rendus); Beckenbach and Radó rediscovered it in 1933 (Trans. AMS 35(3)). The Wikipedia article states the dimension-2 case 'had already been established in 1926 by André Weil'. Background, pre-window; recorded because the problem was solved in dimension 2 decades ago.
events.delivers: The dimension-2 case of the conjecture: the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard surfaces (every Riemannian metric on a disk with K <= 0). Per the Izmestiev-type statement seen in search, the result covers any complete simply connected surface of K <= 0; the Comptes Rendus text was not opened.
events.remains: Dimensions n >= 3 (dimension 3 and 4 handled by later events below; dimensions 5 and up addressed only by the 2026 events).

checked_by.qualification: analysts who independently proved the same surface result
checked_by.what_they_did: Rediscovered the dimension-2 inequality in 1933 (Subharmonic functions and surfaces of negative curvature, Trans. AMS 35(3) pp. 662-674, per a search snippet; not opened)

events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: it proves the inequality in dimension 2.

events.what_happened: Christopher Croke, 'A sharp four dimensional isoperimetric inequality', Comment. Math. Helv. 59 (1984) 187-192. The Wikipedia article credits Croke with the dimension-4 case; Ghomi-Spruck and Chen-Ghomi-Wang's introduction credit it likewise. Pre-window; recorded as a solved case.
events.delivers: The dimension-4 case: the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for domains in Cartan-Hadamard 4-manifolds, equality for balls (per the Wikipedia and Ghomi-Spruck statements; the Croke paper itself was not opened, so no theorem statement is quoted here).
events.remains: Dimensions n = 3 handled by Kleiner (1992) and n = 2 by Weil; n >= 5 open except as per the 2026 events below.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1984; reviewer identifiers Zbl 0552.53017 and MR749103 per an EuDML search snippet

checked_by.who: Author not established in this run (expository article in Séminaire de théorie spectrale et géométrie, vol. 18, 1999-2000, 'Une inégalité isopérimétrique en courbure négative d'après Christopher B. Croke')
checked_by.qualification: expository digest, published in a seminar volume
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a French-language digest of Croke's inequality; seen only as a search result title, not opened

events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: proves the inequality in dimension 4.

events.what_happened: Bruce Kleiner, 'An isoperimetric comparison theorem', Invent. Math. 108 (1992) 37-47 (DOI 10.1007/bf02100598, per search snippet). The Wikipedia article states that 'in dimensions 3 and 4 the conjecture was proved by Bruce Kleiner and Chris Croke'. Kleiner's variational method reduces the problem to a total curvature inequality. Pre-window; recorded as a solved case.
events.delivers: The dimension-3 case of the conjecture, per Wikipedia and Ghomi-Spruck. Scope caveat: a search summary described Kleiner's 1992 sharp inequality as a comparison for 3-manifolds with K <= -1 against hyperbolic balls, which is a different statement from the Euclidean inequality for K <= 0. The Kleiner paper itself was not opened, so the scope is recorded as disputed in 'disputes'.
events.remains: Dimensions n >= 4 except n = 4 (Croke); the 2026 events below address dimension 5 and up.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1992 (per search snippet; not opened)

checked_by.qualification: mathematician who wrote an expository account in the Séminaire de théorie spectrale et géométrie
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote 'Inégalité isopérimétrique en dimension 3 d'après B. Kleiner' (vol. 18, 1999-2000, pp. 59-64), per a search result; not opened

events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: proves it in dimension 3 (per Wikipedia and Ghomi-Spruck), subject to the scope question in 'disputes'.

events.what_happened: Benoît Kloeckner and Greg Kuperberg, 'The Cartan-Hadamard conjecture and the Little Prince', arXiv:1303.3115 (v1 13 Mar 2013; v3 13 Feb 2017). Their abstract gives a unified proof for dimensions 2 and 4 in the zero-curvature case of a generalized conjecture (curvature bounded above by kappa <= 0), partial results for negative curvature, and counterexamples to a naive version in dimension 3. Published in Revista Matemática Iberoamericana (2019) per a search snippet; the journal reference is not on the arXiv page. Pre-window background, recorded because it is an event bearing on the problem's hypotheses.
events.revisions: v1 13 Mar 2013; v2 9 Dec 2014; v3 13 Feb 2017 (current). Journal: Rev. Mat. Iberoam. (2019), per search snippet, not opened.
events.delivers: Unified proof, for n = 2 and n = 4, of the generalized conjecture in the zero-curvature case (kappa = 0), which for n = 4 recovers Croke's result; partial results under negative curvature with a 'candle condition'; and counterexamples to a naive 3-dimensional formulation in which only the diffeomorphism type of a ball is assumed, with boundary area bounded while volume is arbitrarily large (per the abstract and the search summary). The counterexamples are to a formulation without the ambient Cartan-Hadamard hypothesis; the authors use them to justify the hypotheses of the conjecture.
events.remains: The Euclidean inequality for Cartan-Hadamard manifolds in dimensions n >= 3 apart from the cases already known; the negative-curvature generalization is only partly treated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2019, per search snippet linking ems.press DOI 10.4171/rmi/1082; not opened)

events.doubts: The counterexample scope is contested by no one in the sources read, but the 2026 Agnoletto et al. preprint reports a remark that the conjecture is 'false for Riemannian 3-balls' under its hypotheses (search snippet, not verified); the authors' own statement is that the counterexamples concern a naive formulation.
events.direction: Mixed: positive partial results (dimensions 2 and 4 in the flat case, already known) and counterexamples to a naive 3-dimensional formulation that drops the ambient Cartan-Hadamard hypothesis. Per the authors these do not contradict the conjecture as stated with its hypotheses.
events.object: Existence statement: for every epsilon > 0, a Riemannian 3-manifold Ω diffeomorphic to a ball with (1-epsilon)-pinched negative curvature whose boundary area is bounded in terms of epsilon while its volume is arbitrarily large (per the search summary of the abstract). Whether the construction is explicit was not verified.

events.what_happened: Mohammad Ghomi and Joel Spruck, 'Total curvature and the isoperimetric inequality in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds', arXiv:1908.09814 (v1 26 Aug 2019). Abstract (v1, verbatim): 'We prove that the total positive Gauss-Kronecker curvature of any closed hypersurface embedded in a complete simply connected manifold of nonpositive curvature M^n, n >= 2, is bounded below by the volume of the unit sphere in Euclidean space R^n. This yields the optimal isoperimetric inequality for bounded regions of finite perimeter in M, via Kleiner's variational approach, and thus settles the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture.' Georgia Tech announced the work in August 2019 as settling the conjecture 'in all dimensions'. The paper was accepted for publication in J. Geom. Anal. (2022, vol. 32, paper 50, per the author's publication list in a search snippet). A gap in the proof was reported in 2019 and again in March 2020 (see 'doubts').
events.revisions: v1 26 Aug 2019; v2 23 Sep 2019; v3 7 Oct 2019; v4 16 Nov 2019; v5 16 Mar 2020; v6 6 Feb 2021; v7 23 Sep 2021 (current; comments: 'Minor revisions to the last draft; Accepted for publication in J. Geom. Anal'). Ghomi's 30 Sep 2019 reply on the Kalai blog says an updated version fixes the issue then raised; the 22 Mar 2020 blog update says 'a gap in the proof has now been reported'.
events.delivers: As claimed in the v1 abstract: for all n >= 2 the total positive Gauss-Kronecker curvature of a closed embedded hypersurface in a Cartan-Hadamard manifold is at least that of the unit sphere, and via Kleiner's variational argument the optimal isoperimetric inequality for bounded finite-perimeter regions in M, i.e. the full conjecture in all dimensions. Whether the v7/JGA version still delivers the full claim is not established in the sources read; the v7 abstract says only 'develop some applications ... to the isoperimetric problem'.
events.remains: If the claim holds, nothing; if the gap stands, the total-curvature step is open and the isoperimetric inequality in all dimensions is unproven by this event. Later sources (Wheeler 2026; Ghomi-Stavroulakis 2026) describe the total curvature conjecture as open in arbitrary dimension.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication (vol. 32 (2022), paper 50), per the arXiv comments field and a search snippet of the author's publication list. The journal page itself was not opened and it is not established whether the published version closes the gap.

checked_by.qualification: mathematician and blog author; affiliation not checked in this run
checked_by.what_they_did: Posted a digest of the claim on 28 Aug 2019 ('settled the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture!'); did not verify the argument; later posted an update (22 Mar 2020) reporting that 'a gap in the proof has now been reported'

events.doubts: (a) A reader comment of 24 Sep 2019 on the Kalai blog says there appears to be at least one problem in the argument that the authors have ceded; Ghomi replied on 30 Sep 2019 that the updated arXiv version fixes that issue. (b) The 22 Mar 2020 update on the same blog reports 'a gap in the proof has now been reported' without a further citation. (c) A search snippet of the arXiv listing says a corrigendum has been added noting a computational error that 'opens a gap in the proof of the main result' with a plan to fix it in a future revision; the v7 comments field read in this run does not contain that corrigendum sentence, so the two sources conflict. (d) A 2020 talk abstract by Ghomi (search snippet) describes a narrower result under small variation of ambient curvature. (e) The 2026 Chen-Ghomi-Wang abstract uses 'the isoperimetric-profile argument of Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck', so the 2026 dimension 3-9 result depends on the Ghomi-Spruck step; the sources do not say whether the 2020 gap affects it.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims the full inequality in all dimensions n >= 2 (the bullet's own claim), if correct.

events.what_happened: Joseph Hoisington, 'Hypersurfaces, Geodesics and Isoperimetric Inequalities in Cartan-Hadamard Manifolds', arXiv:2111.06860 (12 Nov 2021, single version). Proves an inequality for submanifolds relating geometry to the measure of ambient geodesics they meet; for hypersurfaces an extension of Banchoff-Pohl's isoperimetric inequality; a modified version of Croke's isoperimetric inequality for immersed hypersurfaces; and a sharp quantitative form of Yau's isoperimetric inequality in negative curvature (abstract read verbatim in part). Pre-window neighbouring result, recorded because it bears on the Croke and isoperimetric-inequality strands.
events.delivers: Inequalities for hypersurfaces (and submanifolds) in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds: a Banchoff-Pohl-type isoperimetric inequality, a modified Croke inequality, and a quantitative Yau inequality in negative curvature. These are inequalities about hypersurfaces or modified forms, not the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for domains in CH manifolds as stated in the bullet.
events.remains: The sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for domains in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds in every dimension; the paper does not claim it.
events.direction: Neighbouring result: a different inequality (hypersurface, modified Croke form, Yau-type) that does not decide the bullet's question either way.

events.what_happened: Mohammad Ghomi and John Ioannis Stavroulakis, 'A local isoperimetric inequality for balls with nonpositive curvature', arXiv:2505.11971 (v1 17 May 2025; v2 19 Feb 2026, current). Abstract (verbatim in part): 'small perturbations of the metric of a ball in Euclidean n-space to metrics with nonpositive curvature do not reduce the isoperimetric ratio'; 'the isoperimetric ratio is preserved only if the perturbation corresponds to a homothety of the ball'; 'These results establish a sharp local version of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture.'
events.revisions: v1 17 May 2025; v2 19 Feb 2026 (current). The v1 text (search snippet) mentions the Rauch comparison theorem and a generalization to curvature bounded by k <= 0.
events.delivers: A local statement: for metrics on a Euclidean ball that are C^2-close to the Euclidean metric and have nonpositive curvature, the isoperimetric ratio is at least the Euclidean value, with equality only for isometric Euclidean balls.
events.remains: The global statement: domains in arbitrary Cartan-Hadamard manifolds, not only small perturbations of a ball.
events.direction: Partial support for the conjecture in a local, perturbative class; does not decide the global question.

events.what_happened: Ghomi and Stavroulakis, 'Total curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds', arXiv:2601.13280 (19 Jan 2026). Abstract (verbatim in part): 'if the curvature of a Cartan-Hadamard n-manifold is constant near a convex hypersurface Γ, then the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature G(Γ) is not less than that of any convex hypersurface nested inside Γ'; 'It follows that G(Γ) is bounded below by the volume of the unit sphere in Euclidean space.'
events.delivers: A total-curvature inequality for convex hypersurfaces under the hypothesis that the ambient curvature is constant near the hypersurface, extending Borbély's monotonicity theorem in hyperbolic space. Conditional on that constant-curvature hypothesis; the paper does not claim the isoperimetric inequality for general CH manifolds.
events.remains: The isoperimetric inequality without the constant-curvature hypothesis; the total-curvature bound for general ambient curvature.
events.doubts: The paper is restricted to ambient curvature constant near Γ; it is the same total-curvature inequality type that Ghomi-Spruck (2019) and Wheeler (2026) treat as the open route. Per a search snippet the paper cites Ghomi-Spruck as a reference for the conjecture rather than a resolution; the paper's abstract as fetched does not say so.
events.direction: Partial: a conditional total-curvature bound, supporting the conjecture only under constant-curvature hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Mohammad Ghomi, 'Isoperimetric and total curvature inequalities in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity', arXiv (23 May 2026, single version). Abstract (verbatim in part): 'Using the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we establish a sharp inequality for the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds M^n with nullity index at least n-3. Consequently, the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality extends to M^n, which proves the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for these spaces.'
events.delivers: The Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity index at least n-3, in every dimension n for which that condition is meaningful. The authors say this proves the conjecture 'for these spaces'. The class is restricted: for n = 4 it means nullity at least 1 (a search summary's inference); the abstract gives no separate dimension range.
events.remains: Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity index below n-3; so the general conjecture in every dimension is not settled by this paper.
events.doubts: Restricted class by hypothesis; no checks found. The sentence 'Consequently ... proves the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for these spaces' is a claim about a restricted class; the full text was not read.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture within the nullity-class: claims the inequality for all Cartan-Hadamard manifolds of nullity at least n-3.

events.what_happened: Mohammad Ghomi (sole author), 'Total curvature and isoperimetric inequalities in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds', arXiv:2608.12020 (12 Aug 2026, single version). Abstract (verbatim in part): 'We establish a sharp lower bound for the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature of convex hypersurfaces'; 'The bound holds in all dimensions when the diameter is small relative to the curvature scale, and in dimensions 4 and 5 without any restriction on the diameter, provided that the pinching is sufficiently tight'; 'As an application, we obtain the isoperimetric inequality of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in dimension 5 under sufficiently pinched curvature.'
events.delivers: In dimension 5, the isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard manifolds whose sectional curvature is sufficiently pinched; in dimensions 4 and 5 a total-curvature bound under tight pinching; in all dimensions a total-curvature bound for small diameter relative to curvature scale. The paper does not claim the isoperimetric inequality in dimension 4 or the unpinched dimension-5 case.
events.remains: Unpinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds in dimension 5 (covered by the later Chen-Ghomi-Wang event); all of dimension 4 and n >= 6 by this paper's isoperimetric claim.
events.doubts: Restricted by pinching; the dimension-5 claim is conditional on a 'sufficiently pinched' hypothesis whose constant is not given in the abstract; no checks found.
events.direction: Partial: supports the conjecture in dimension 5 under sufficient pinching; does not decide the unpinched case.

events.what_happened: Shibing Chen, Mohammad Ghomi and Peng Wang, 'The Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in dimension five', arXiv:2609.11005 (submitted 10 Sep 2026; single version, 19 pages; math.DG, cross-listed math.MG). Abstract (verbatim in part, arXiv abs page): 'the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality holds for domains in complete simply connected Riemannian 5-manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature, which establishes the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in that dimension'; 'Our method also gives a new proof in dimension 3.' Theorem 1.1 (HTML): for bounded Ω with finite perimeter |Γ| and |Ω| > 0, |Γ|^5/|Ω|^4 >= |S^4|^5/|B^5|^4, with equality only if Ω is isometric to a Euclidean ball. The stated method: a sharp inequality for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces via integrals over pairs of boundary points (in the style of Banchoff-Pohl) with Jacobi-field estimates along geodesic chords; the final step uses Kleiner's isoperimetric-profile argument (per search snippet of the paper; the abstract of the follow-up paper states this dependence).
events.revisions: v1 10 Sep 2026 only (arXiv listing as read on 10 Oct 2026).
events.delivers: The sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for bounded domains of finite perimeter and positive volume in complete simply connected Riemannian 5-manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature, with equality only for Euclidean balls. Covers dimension 5 in full (the bullet's statement restricted to n = 5). Also, per the abstract, a new proof in dimension 3.
events.remains: Dimensions n >= 6 (and dimension 4, which is already known by Croke); the generalized form with curvature bounded above by a negative constant (not part of the bullet's statement).
events.doubts: (a) Single arXiv version, not in a journal, no referee report or expert verification found in any search (Lean search and news search returned nothing for this result). (b) The authors' own acknowledgement says the manuscript was prepared with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT) and that the authors 'reviewed all AI-assisted content'; the role of those tools in the mathematics is not stated. (c) Agnoletto et al. (arXiv:2609.17093, 15 Sep 2026) state in a remark that the authors of the Chen-Ghomi-Wang papers 'are not yet familiar with their entire proofs since they're extremely recent'; that is a third party's report of the authors' own remark, not a check. (d) The final step uses the isoperimetric-profile argument of Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck; the Ghomi-Spruck 2019 argument had a reported gap (2019 reader comment; 22 Mar 2020 blog update). The sources read do not establish whether the dimension-5 proof depends on the disputed step. (e) Ghomi's own pinched-curvature dimension-5 result (2608.12020) was posted a month earlier and reaches the same conclusion under pinching; no conflict was found.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims the inequality holds in dimension 5 for all Cartan-Hadamard 5-manifolds (no pinching).

It does not say whether it contributed mathematics (ideas, proof steps, checking) or only writing and presentation. The authors add that they 'reviewed all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility for the final manuscript'.

events.what_happened: Glen Wheeler, 'The Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetric inequality under controlled variation of curvature', arXiv:2609.14505 (submitted 13 Sep 2026; sole author; single version). Abstract (verbatim in part): 'We prove the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture (the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality) in every dimension, assuming that the sectional curvature is pinched relative to a reference radius of curvature.' Theorem 1.1 (HTML): for each n >= 2 there are constants eps_n and c_n such that manifolds with (eps_n, c_n)-controlled variation of curvature satisfy the inequality for every bounded set of finite perimeter and positive volume. The pinching in Definition 1.2 is of negative curvature: -kappa(x) <= sec <= -(1-eta) kappa(x). Method: control of the convex hull of a quotient minimiser at mean-curvature scale, compared against the surplus in the normalised hyperbolic isoperimetric profile. The paper states that it does not need the total-curvature bound of the earlier approach.
events.delivers: The Euclidean isoperimetric inequality in every dimension n >= 2, but only for manifolds whose sectional curvature is pinched (negatively, with controlled variation of the reference radius) in the stated sense. Unpinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds are not covered by the theorem as stated in the sections read.
events.remains: Cartan-Hadamard manifolds that are not controlled-pinched, in every dimension. The paper says its main theorem matters mainly for n >= 6 because dimensions 3 to 5 are already known without pinching (the paper's remark).
events.doubts: Single preprint, no journal, no referee or expert check found. The pinching hypothesis is restrictive and the paper's own framing (matters mainly for n >= 6) concedes that the lower dimensions are covered elsewhere. Its proof was read only in the HTML sections the fetch returned; the full argument was not checked.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture in every dimension but only under controlled pinching; the bullet's unpinched statement is not decided.

events.what_happened: Marcos Agnoletto, Márcio Fabiano da Silva, Stefano Nardulli and Reinaldo Resende, 'A proof of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for small volumes under a Ricci curvature lower bound', arXiv:2609.17093 (v1 15 Sep 2026; v2 21 Sep 2026). Abstract (verbatim in part, v2): 'We prove the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, also known as the Aubin conjecture, in the small volume regime under a lower Ricci curvature bound'; 'We also reduce the proof of the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture to establishing rigidity in the equality case.' Remark 1.7 discusses the Chen-Ghomi-Wang papers.
events.revisions: v1 15 Sep 2026; v2 21 Sep 2026 (current). Per the version note: v2 'removed the Ricci lower bound from a main theorem, added a new section, updated the literature, and revised the introduction'. The v2 abstract as fetched still states the Ricci lower bound, so the two sources conflict on scope.
events.delivers: For small volumes (for all n >= 2), under sectional curvature bounded above by a nonpositive constant and a lower Ricci bound, the isoperimetric profile is at least that of the model space; for model curvature 0 this gives the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for small volumes under the Ricci hypothesis. Also a reduction of the full generalized conjecture to a rigidity statement in the equality case.
events.remains: Large volumes, and the Euclidean statement without a Ricci lower bound, in dimensions n >= 3 (per the abstract's own reduction, the full conjecture reduces to rigidity in the equality case, which is not claimed as proved).
events.doubts: Scope change between versions (the Ricci hypothesis is said to have been removed from one main theorem in v2, while the abstract still states it); no referee or expert check found. The paper's own statement (search snippet of Remark 1.7) is that the authors of the Chen-Ghomi-Wang papers were not yet familiar with their entire proofs; this is a third-party paper's comment, not a check.
events.direction: Cuts for the generalized conjecture in the small-volume regime under a Ricci bound; for the bullet's Euclidean statement it is a restricted (small-volume, Ricci-bounded) result.

events.what_happened: Shibing Chen, Mohammad Ghomi and Peng Wang, 'The isoperimetric inequality and CMC hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds', arXiv:2609.20517 (submitted 17 Sep 2026; single version; math.DG, cross-listed math.MG; 35 pages). Abstract (verbatim, arXiv abs page): 'We show that the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality holds for domains in complete simply connected Riemannian n-manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature, 3 <= n <= 9, which establishes the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in these dimensions.' 'The main step is a sharp inequality for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces, proved via integrals over pairs of boundary points, together with estimates for Jacobi fields along geodesic chords of the boundary.' 'The isoperimetric-profile argument of Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck completes the proof.' Theorem 1.1 (HTML): for a bounded set Ω in M^n with 3 <= n <= 9, |Γ|^n / |Ω|^(n-1) >= |S^(n-1)|^n / |B^n|^(n-1), equality only if Ω is isometric to a Euclidean ball. Theorem 1.2: for a compact embedded hypersurface of constant mean curvature H > 0 in the same range, |Γ| >= ((n-1)/H)^(n-1) |S^(n-1)|, equality only if Γ bounds a Euclidean ball of radius (n-1)/H. The introduction says the paper gives 'a unified proof of these results for n >= 3 by refining the approach' of the authors' dimension-five paper, and that 'in a sequel, we will show that our methods can be refined to obtain the generalized form of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in dimensions n=4 and 5'.
events.revisions: v1 17 Sep 2026 only (39 KB arXiv listing as read on 10 Oct 2026).
events.delivers: The sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for bounded sets in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds of dimension 3 to 9 (Theorem 1.1, equality only for Euclidean balls), per the authors' abstract and theorem statement. Dimensions 3 to 5 overlap with earlier results; dimensions 6 to 9 are new if the proof holds. The Wikipedia article describes this as a unified proof for dimensions 3 to 9.
events.remains: Dimensions n >= 10 in the Euclidean statement; the generalized form (curvature bounded above by a negative constant, comparison with hyperbolic balls), which the paper says is deferred to a sequel and is not part of the bullet's statement.
events.doubts: (a) Single arXiv version, not in a journal; no referee report, expert check, or formal verification found. The Wikipedia article reports the claim as a proof but that is not an expert check. (b) The abstract relies on 'the isoperimetric-profile argument of Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck'; the Ghomi-Spruck argument had a reported gap in 2019-2020 (see the Ghomi-Spruck event), and the sources read do not say whether the gap is repaired or whether it affects this step. (c) The companion dimension-5 paper's AI acknowledgement (Claude, ChatGPT) is reported as present in this paper too by a search snippet, but the fetched text did not reach the acknowledgements; not verified here. (d) Agnoletto et al. (2609.17093) state that the authors were 'not yet familiar with their entire proofs since they're extremely recent'; that is a third party's remark about the authors, not a check.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims the sharp inequality for bounded sets in every Cartan-Hadamard n-manifold with 3 <= n <= 9.

events.what_happened: Two manuscripts, both dated 23 September 2026. (1) 'Generalized Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetry and Euclidean equality rigidity' claims that for a complete simply connected smooth Riemannian n-manifold (n >= 2) with sectional curvature at most kappa <= 0, every measurable set E with finite volume and finite ambient perimeter P_g(E) satisfies P_g(E) >= I_{sqrt(-kappa)}(vol(E)), where I_b is the isoperimetric profile of the model space of curvature -b^2 (Theorem 1.1). At kappa = 0 this is P_g(E) >= n omega_n^(1/n) vol(E)^((n-1)/n), equivalently P^n >= n^n omega_n vol^(n-1). It also claims an equality classification at kappa = 0 (Theorem 1.2): for bounded E with 0 < vol(E) < infinity and P_g(E) < infinity, equality in the Euclidean bound holds if and only if E agrees up to null sets with an open region whose induced metric is that of a round Euclidean ball, and the ambient manifold outside that region need not be flat. (2) 'Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces' claims that every compactly supported integral n-cycle T (n >= 2) in a proper CAT(0) space bounds a compactly supported integral current S with M(S) <= c_n M(T)^((n+1)/n), where c_n = 1/((n+1) s_n^(1/n)) and s_n = area of the unit n-sphere, and that this coefficient is optimal (Theorem 1 of that paper). Its Cartan-Hadamard corollary says that for a Cartan-Hadamard manifold of dimension d >= 3 and a bounded smooth domain Omega, area(boundary of Omega) >= d omega_d^(1/d) vol(Omega)^((d-1)/d). The filling theorem is applied to the integration current of Omega, and top-dimensional constancy gives S = [[Omega]]. The text says the same inequality extends to relatively compact finite-perimeter sets with ambient perimeter, and it handles d = 2 separately by the classical disk inequality (Section 8).

machine_checked.scope:
The formalization proves the sharp Euclidean filling inequality for every compactly supported integral $n$-cycle in a proper $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, for $n\ge2$. It constructs a compactly supported integral filling whose mass is at most $C_n$ times the boundary mass to the power $(n+1)/n$, where $C_n$ is the Euclidean isoperimetric coefficient. Integer multiplicities and the ambient dimension are unrestricted.

A second statement proves that this coefficient is optimal by giving, in Euclidean space, a cycle for which every compactly supported integral filling has at least that mass. This yields the selected integral-current form of the Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture.

events.doubts: Manuscript 2's abstract restricts the Cartan-Hadamard claim to dimensions at least three, but its introduction and Section 8 extend it to every d >= 2 by the classical disk inequality, so the abstract understates the body. Its extension of the domain corollary to finite-perimeter sets is said to follow 'verbatim' from the smooth case, with citations and no separate check. Its foundations theorem (Theorem 'current-background') is recorded from the literature, not proved. Manuscript 1's introduction summarises key steps (the completed square, 'balancing ... forces a first-order identity', the spherical-coordinate variations) in prose, and the full arguments are in the body. In its dimension-two equality argument (Section 8), the periodicity of a boundary component is justified in part by the remark that it 'can also be seen by continuing an oriented arclength chart', with no full proof. Manuscript 1's dimension-three comparison rests entirely on a 1992 citation, not on argument in the paper.; conditional on: Manuscript 1 relies on cited results for the n = 2 and n = 3 cases: the Weil-Bol disk inequality in the Chavel-Feldman form (n = 2) and Kleiner's Theorem 2 (n = 3, cited with page 38). It also uses Gueneysu-Pallara's strict smooth approximation, cited as 'Theorem 2.12 in the author preprint'. Its regularity steps use Ghomi-Spruck Lemma 7.2(i),(ii) for obstacle regularity, Antonelli-Pasqualetto-Pozzetta Corollary 1.6 for almost-minimizer regularity in the equality part, and Brezis-Lieb splitting, with the Aubin-Talenti constant. The hypersurface Sobolev inequality, the confined profile, the n >= 4 comparison, the cutoff passage to infinite volume and the equality rigidity are proved in the paper. Manuscript 2's domain corollary depends on its own integral filling theorem, which is proved by induction on the cycle dimension. That theorem's foundations are Ambrosio-Kirchheim, Wenger, Kirchheim and Sturm's CAT(0) variance inequality, which the text records as standard and cites. The integration-current representation of finite-perimeter sets is cited to Simon 2014, and the d = 2 case is cited to the classical disk inequality (Izmestiev 2014). Manuscript 2 does not depend on manuscript 1.
events.direction: proves the conjecture in all dimensions (kappa = 0 case); equality classified for bounded sets
events.object: No counterexample and no explicit object for the Cartan-Hadamard problem. Euclidean balls are the extremal sets; manuscript 2 (Section 8) checks that the boundary of a Euclidean ball B_R in R^(n+1) attains the filling coefficient. That concerns the filling constant in Euclidean space, not a construction on a Cartan-Hadamard manifold.

disputes.summary: Ghomi and Spruck (2019) claimed to settle the conjecture in all dimensions n >= 2 (abstract v1: 'thus settles the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture'; Georgia Tech news: 'settles the conjecture in all dimensions'). Later sources do not treat the general case as settled: Wheeler (13 Sep 2026) and Ghomi-Stavroulakis (2026) describe the total curvature conjecture as open in arbitrary dimension and the Ghomi-Spruck route as depending on it; the 2026 dimension 3-9 paper uses the Ghomi-Spruck profile argument; the 2020 blog update reports a gap.

Ghomi-Spruck gap: a reader comment (24 Sep 2019) and a blog update (22 Mar 2020: 'a gap in the proof has now been reported') versus Ghomi's reply (30 Sep 2019) that an updated version fixes the issue. A search snippet of the arXiv listing reports a corrigendum for 'a computational error which opens a gap in the proof of the main result'; the v7 comments field read here does not contain that corrigendum. Which version the JGA publication reflects is not established.

Kleiner (1992) scope: Wikipedia and Ghomi-Spruck present Kleiner's result as the dimension-3 Cartan-Hadamard case; a search summary described Kleiner's 1992 sharp inequality as a comparison for 3-manifolds with curvature <= -1 against hyperbolic balls. The Kleiner paper was not opened, so the scope is not settled here.

Dimension-5 claim: Chen-Ghomi-Wang (10 Sep 2026) is the first claim for dimension 5 in this record. Ghomi's pinched-curvature paper (12 Aug 2026) reached the dimension-5 isoperimetric inequality under sufficient pinching earlier in the same month; the two do not conflict, since one is pinched and the other is not. Wheeler (13 Sep 2026) and Agnoletto et al. (15 Sep 2026) both cite the Chen-Ghomi-Wang dimension-5 claim.

summary: The problem has moved since January 2024, but only through preprints from August to September 2026, none yet refereed, and the central claims are dimension-specific. Chen, Ghomi and Wang (arXiv:2609.11005, 10 Sep 2026) claim the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard 5-manifolds, read in full from the HTML version (Theorem 1.1, equality only for balls); their companion arXiv:2609.20517 (17 Sep 2026) claims it for 3 <= n <= 9 (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 read from the HTML version, which is truncated before the end). The Wikipedia article reports both as proofs and describes a unified proof for dimensions 3 to 9. Their AI disclosure is the clearest AI item: the 2609.11005 HTML acknowledgement reads 'The AI tools Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI) were used in the preparation of this manuscript. The authors have reviewed all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility for the final manuscript.' That sentence does not say whether the tools contributed mathematics, so I recorded both names with the quote and did not infer a load-bearing role. For 2609.20517, a search snippet reports the same acknowledgement, but the fetched HTML did not reach the acknowledgements section, so that is unverified and I recorded no systems for it. A third paper (Agnoletto, da Silva, Nardulli, Resende, arXiv:2609.17093, 15 Sep 2026) reports the AI disclosure 'Publicly available LLMs were used to improve the grammar and flow of the introduction' in its own text; I recorded it as proofreading with no named system. Several other events are restricted: Wheeler (arXiv:2609.14505, 13 Sep 2026) claims all dimensions under a controlled negative pinching; Ghomi (arXiv:2608.12020, 12 Aug 2026) gives dimension 5 under sufficient pinching; Ghomi (arXiv:2605.24638, 23 May 2026) covers nullity index at least n-3; Ghomi and Stavroulakis give a local perturbation theorem (arXiv:2505.11971, May 2025, v2 Feb 2026) and a conditional total-curvature bound (arXiv:2601.13280, Jan 2026); Agnoletto et al. give small volumes under a Ricci lower bound for the generalized conjecture. Older events: Weil (dimension 2, 1926), Croke (dimension 4, 1984), Kleiner (dimension 3, 1992), and Kloeckner-Kuperberg (2013), which gives partial results and counterexamples to a naive 3-dimensional formulation without the ambient hypothesis. The 2019 Ghomi-Spruck claim of all dimensions (arXiv:1908.09814) is the older contested event: it was accepted by the Journal of Geometric Analysis (2022, per the author's list, journal not opened), but a gap was reported in 2019 and again on 22 March 2020, and a search snippet of the arXiv listing mentions a corrigendum that the v7 page I read does not show. The dimension 3-9 papers depend on the Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck isoperimetric-profile argument, so whether the 2019 gap is repaired matters for them; the sources read do not settle this. Later sources, Wheeler and Ghomi-Stavroulakis, still describe the total curvature route as open in general. Close call 1: whether the 2026 dimension 3-9 claim counts as a resolution of the bullet is a question of verification, not scope: it is the bullet's own statement for those dimensions, but it is an unrefereed preprint depending on a step with a reported gap. Close call 2: whether the Ghomi-Spruck 2019 claim is current or superseded. Close call 3: the AI role in the Chen-Ghomi-Wang manuscripts; the acknowledgement names the tools and says they were 'used in the preparation of this manuscript', which is consistent with proofreading and with mathematical contribution, and the record does not decide between these. The AI search turned up no other AI-credited work on this problem: the Wikipedia list of AI mathematical discoveries (opened, latest entries October 2026) has no Cartan-Hadamard entry, and its only Hadamard match concerns Hadamard matrices. No Lean or Coq formalisation of the Cartan-Hadamard statement was found; the Lean search returned only a planar isoperimetric formalisation.
competing_reading: The 2026 claims are likely right and the status should move to 'proved in dimensions 3 to 9, and in dimension 5 alone for the unpinched case' on the strength of: Ghomi and Chen are experienced geometers, the dimension-5 paper is 19 pages with a stated proof strategy and an equality characterisation, the dimension 3-9 paper is 35 pages, Wikipedia already reports the claims as proofs, and Wheeler reaches the all-dimension conclusion under pinching by a different method. On this reading the Ghomi-Spruck 2019 gap is a historical point, since the 2026 proofs use the profile argument rather than the disputed total-curvature theorem, and the AI acknowledgement is a disclosure of tools used in preparation, not evidence of load-bearing AI mathematics. The opposite reading: none of the 2026 items has been refereed; the dimension 3-9 result inherits the Kleiner and Ghomi-Spruck profile step whose total-curvature input had a reported gap; the authors' own AI disclosure is non-specific; and the strongest statement in the record (all dimensions) is still contested. On that reading the general problem remains open and the 2026 events establish dimension 5 (and possibly 3 to 9) only conditionally on verification.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Journal acceptance or referee reports for arXiv:2609.11005 and arXiv:2609.20517. (2) Whether the 2022 Journal of Geometric Analysis version of Ghomi-Spruck (arXiv:1908.09814) closes the 2020 gap, and whether the 2609.20517 profile step depends on that theorem. (3) The full text of 2609.20517 (acknowledgements and theorem proofs), to confirm the AI disclosure and whether it names what the tools did. (4) The authors' description of what Claude and ChatGPT did in the mathematics, if any. (5) An expert verification or a Lean formalisation of the dimension-5 argument. (6) Whether Wheeler's controlled-pinching theorem is refereed and whether it covers unpinched manifolds (it does not, as read). (7) Full text of the Kleiner 1992 paper, to settle the dimension-3 scope.

judgement.why: The statement asks whether the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality holds in every Cartan-Hadamard manifold, all dimensions, so dimension-specific or hypothesis-restricted results (Weil, Croke, Kleiner, Ghomi nullity/pinched, Wheeler pinched, Agnoletto small volume, Chen-Ghomi-Wang dims 5 and 3-9) are cases. The local perturbative theorem concerns only metrics near a Euclidean ball, a changed question (variant); the conditional total-curvature bound proves no isoperimetric statement (none); Kloeckner-Kuperberg's counterexamples drop the ambient hypothesis (variant). Ghomi-Spruck 2019 claimed the whole but carries a specific reported gap, a corrigendum snippet, a retreated v7 abstract and later work by Ghomi himself treating the question as open, so I set it knocked_down despite JGA acceptance; this keeps it from making the problem open_stale. The OpenAI repository's two manuscripts claim all dimensions; only a Lean build of the filling theorem backs them, which is not digestion (F7), so unreviewed, credible absent any identified error. Its README says the model obtained the results: generated. The Chen-Ghomi-Wang acknowledgement ('used in the preparation of this manuscript') names no mathematical contribution, so none.
judgement.doubts: Ghomi-Spruck knocked_down rests partly on a search snippet of a corrigendum and on the JGA version not having been opened; if the published version closes the gap it would be digested-whole pre-snapshot. The OpenAI manuscripts are 8 days old with no human reader; the Lean scope covers the CAT(0) filling theorem, and the passage from filling to the domain inequality is not formalized as recorded. The Chen-Ghomi-Wang dims 3-9 AI acknowledgement was not read. The ghomi-stavroulakis-2025-local call (variant vs case) was close.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
